# Customer License Cosmos Schema

## Fields

Key | Template | Description
--- | --- | ---
PartitionKey | {customerID}/CustomerLicense/{product} | By partitioning Customer Licenses by Customer ID and Product, we can efficiently query for all licenses for a specific customer and product. It is very rare that we would ever query for customer licenses across multiple customers or products at any given time, but quite common that we will want to query amongst the licenses for a single customer-product combo.
ID | {licenseeType}:{licenseeID} | The ID field is a composed of licensee type and licensee ID. In the case that we want to pull back a single customer license, we will know the licensee type and ID (in addition to all the parameters in the PartitionKey), so we will be able to use a point read to get the license.
CustomerId | {number} | The ID of the customer that owns the license.
Product | {string} | The product that the license is for.
Licensee | | The object that has been granted the license.
Licensee.Type | {string} | The type of the licensee. Most often "User", but this will expand to include other types.
Licensee.ID | {string} | The ID of the licensee of the given type, unique when combined with Licensee.Type.
Licensee.GlobalID | {string} | (deprecated) The Global ID of the object generated by Rails in the monolith. We were experimenting with this to see if it would make querying easier within the monolith, but performance was not great and we have since moved away from this.
Enablements | | An array of objects that represent the enablements that have caused this license to be granted.
Enablements.[].Type | {string} | The business object type of the enablement. This maps to Models in the monolith, but the value used doesn't directly match the monolith model name. This is usually an org, a team, or a repo.
Enablements.[].Reason | {string} | The reason that explains the association between the licensee and the enablement type. For example "organizationMembership" or "repoCollaborator".
Enablements.[].EnablementIDs | {number[]} | An array of the unique IDs of the enablement objects that contribute to this enablement. For example, if the Enablement.Type is "repo" and the Enablement.Reason is "repoCollaborator", then this array will contain the unique ID of all private repos that the licensee is a collaborator on.
ExpiresAt | {number} | The 64-bit Unix timestamp in seconds that the license will expire. The maximum value supported by protobuf is 253402300799 (which is 9999-12-31 23:59:59 UTC). If the license does not expire, this field will be set to 253402300799. For metered customers, when the last enablement is removed this value gets set to the end of the month.

## ID and Licensee.ID Construction

The `ID` field and `Licensee.ID` are constructed based on `Licensee.Type`:

- **`LicenseeTypeUser`**:
  - **ID Field**: `user:{licenseeID}`
  - **LicenseeID**: The dotcom user ID.
- **`LicenseeTypeEnterpriseServerUser`**:
    - **ID Field**: `enterprise-server-user:{licenseeID}`
    - **LicenseeID**: A hash of the user's normalized primary email (if available), or the user's enterprise installation user account ID (if the email is not available).

This construction ensures that each licensee is uniquely identified and allows for efficient retrieval of licenses.

## Sample Document

```json
{
    "partitionKey": "1/CustomerLicense/sdlc",
    "id": "user:5966",
    "CustomerId": 1,
    "Product": "sdlc",
    "Licensee": {
        "Type": "user",
        "ID": "5966",
        "GlobalID": "gid://git-hub/User/5966"
    },
    "Enablements": [
        {
            "Type": "org",
            "Reason": "organizationMembership",
            "EnablementIDs": [
                4
            ]
        }
    ],
    "ExpiresAt": 253402300799,
    "_rid": "U+xYAK9bnf8VAAAAAAAAAA==",
    "_self": "dbs/U+xYAA==/colls/U+xYAK9bnf8=/docs/U+xYAK9bnf8VAAAAAAAAAA==/",
    "_etag": "\"3a00adda-0000-0700-0000-664e48420000\"",
    "_attachments": "attachments/",
    "_ts": 1716406338
}
```
